zh: 3. 当代前历史

en: Pre-history is, by definition, a past that escapes any chronology. If we sought to identify it with any epoch, however remote, we would only ever grasp an uncertain, poorly documented and fragmentary history. But nothing truly pre-historical. The attempt to situate the absolute past,
-history, within the course of time, leads to a

. As long as I can say that something happened, and when, I am talking about a historical period; to get a grip on pre-history, I must, then, refer back to a previous period; but this one, too, has a ‘something’ and a ‘when’; so I must keep going ever further
back; yet every fresh effort results in yet another checkmate. Indeed, the concept of pre-history has something in common with the original
re-evoked by the mythical-ritual symbol. In both cases, there is no help to be found in the calendar. The anteriority of pre-history, just like that of the
, does not concern a myriad of particular events; rather, it is the anteriority that we usually attribute to an
condition, a fundamental mode of existence, an immovable background.
zh: 依照定义，前历史是一种逃避一切年代定位的过去。如果我们试图把它等同于任何时代，无论多么遥远，都只能把握一段不确定、记录贫乏且支离破碎的历史，而不是真正的前历史。试图把绝对过去——前历史——安置在时间进程之内，会导致无穷倒退。只要我还能说某件事发生了，并且说出它何时发生，我谈论的就是一个历史时期；为了把握前历史，我就必须回指更早时期。但那个时期同样有它的‘某事’与‘某时’，于是我必须不断向后追溯，而每一次新的努力都再次陷入死局。事实上，前历史概念同神话—仪式符号所重现的原初 illud tempus 有某种共同之处。两种情形中，历法都帮不上忙。前历史的在先性，同 illud tempus 的在先性一样，并不涉及无数特殊事件；它是我们通常归给先天条件、根本存在方式或不可移动背景的那种在先性。

en: So let us turn to a thesis that we caught a glimpse of in the second part of the book. Pre-history coincides with the situation of
and
in which we find the living body that does not dispose of a pre-fixed and immutable environment. This original situation is constantly attested to anew by our possession of generic

(linguistic competence, labour-power, memory, etc.): these make up for our lack of specialised instincts, opposing their own plasticity to the indeterminacy of life’s context. Faculties, the different types of potential, relentlessly reaffirm the uncertainty and the lacunae inherent within disoriented existence: preliminary or
uncertainty and lacunae, which precede any act or action we undertake.
zh: 现在让我们转向本书第二部分曾经瞥见的一个论题。前历史同迷失方向和犹疑的处境重合；没有预先固定且不可变化之环境的活的身体，正处于这种处境。我们拥有一般官能——语言能力、劳动力、记忆等等——这一事实，不断重新证明这种原初处境：这些官能弥补专门本能的缺失，以自身可塑性对抗生命语境的不确定性。官能、各种类型的潜能不断重申迷失方向之生存所内含的不确定与缺口：它们是先行或古老的不确定与缺口，先于我们从事的任何实现或行动。

en: There is no potential that is not, in itself, pre-historic. And vice versa: there is no discourse on the primordial that does not concern potential. It suffices, here, to remember that the only philosophical reconnaissance of pre-history was the study of the

, developed with extraordinary intensity during the last decades of the eighteenth century. It goes without saying that the ‘origin’ in question does not consist of certain rudimentary phrases uttered at the dawn of time, but is wholly the same as the
to articulate any phrase, with the simple

capacity-to-speak. Occupying themselves with this faculty or potential, Rousseau, Maupertuis, Hamann and especially Herder became the chroniclers of an incalculable past which seems to precede any historical event, exegetists of the
in which ‘everything was possible … types were not fixed and forms remained fluid’.
zh: 没有任何潜能本身不是前历史的。反过来也一样：没有任何关于原初之物的论述不涉及潜能。这里只需记得，对前历史唯一一次哲学探察，是十八世纪最后几十年以非凡强度展开的语言起源研究。不言而喻，所论‘起源’并非时间黎明时说出的某些粗陋句子，而是同分节任何句子的官能、同单纯的言说能力完全相同。卢梭、莫佩尔蒂、哈曼，尤其赫尔德，在探讨这种官能或潜能时，成为一种无法计算之过去的编年史家；这种过去仿佛先于一切历史事件。他们也成为 illud tempus 的释经者；在那个时间，‘一切皆有可能……类型尚未固定，形式仍在流动’。

en: . The intimate link between pre-history and the origin of language is also apparent from Hegel’s

children: Lectures on the Philosophy of History

en: . Here he affirms that there are historical facts only where there is a historiography up to the task of narrating them; and there is only historiography where there is the state.

For Hegel, life before the state is pre-historic life. But what is it that characterises the long wait for the state, the period prior to history properly speaking? Hegel repeatedly gives the same direct response: ‘the extension and organic growth of the empire of articulate sounds’.
The
of language – its coming into being – is pre-historic. The discovery of Sanskrit ‘as of a new world’
both brings us a little closer to the framework of all languages and casts light on populations whose ‘tradition reaches beyond the record of the founding of the State’.
Yet this does not take us away from the fact that the origins of language itself ‘remain involved in the obscurity of a voiceless past’,
that however variegated and tumultuous, the experiences of pre-state peoples have not ‘given rise to History’.
zh: 释论。前历史与语言起源之间的紧密联系，也显现在黑格尔《历史哲学讲演录》中。他在其中断言，只有当一种史学足以叙述事实时，历史事实才存在；而只有国家存在时，史学才存在。
对黑格尔而言，国家以前的生活是前历史生活。但对国家的漫长等待、严格意义上的历史以前的时期，是由什么刻画的？黑格尔一再给出同一个直接回答：‘有分节声音之王国的扩展与有机生长’。
语言的开端——它的形成——属于前历史。梵语‘仿佛一个新世界’
的发现，既使我们更接近一切语言的框架，也照亮那些‘传统延伸到国家奠基记录之外’
的人群。然而，这仍不能改变如下事实：语言本身的起源‘始终笼罩在无声过去的晦暗中’
；前国家民族的经验无论多么丰富多彩、动荡不安，都没有‘产生历史’。

en: The ‘precociousness’ of language with regard to the state, which Hegel insistently emphasises in his
, is explored in detail in the first chapter of the

, in his discussion of that ‘sensible consciousness’ which limits itself to using a handful of pronouns and deictic adverbs: ‘this’, ‘I’, ‘now’, ‘here’. According to Hegel, these only apparently ingenuous words fully demonstrate the theoretical refinement of language, or its ‘divine nature’. As we know, the ‘sensible consciousness’ is still ignorant of ethical-political relations, the fight for recognition, mastery and servitude. It impersonates only ‘the extension and organic growth of the empire of articulate sounds’: language without the state, prior to the state. The first chapter of the
is, among other things, a
zh: 黑格尔在《历史哲学》中反复强调语言相对于国家的‘早熟’，而《精神现象学》第一章在讨论‘感性意识’时详细考察了这一点；这种意识只使用少量代词和指示副词：‘这个’、‘我’、‘现在’、‘这里’。依照黑格尔的看法，这些只在表面上显得天真的词，充分展示语言的理论精致性或‘神圣本性’。我们知道，‘感性意识’尚不了解伦理—政治关系，不了解争取承认的斗争、主奴关系。它所体现的只是‘有分节声音之王国的扩展与有机生长’：没有国家、先于国家的语言。《精神现象学》第一章同时也是一篇前历史论。

en: Pre-history is an essential, unavoidable aspect of

lived moment. The preliminary situation of disorientation and uncertainty, connected to the lack of any unvarying environmental niche, never fails to make itself felt. Moreover, it establishes – even in its own time – the fact that each single

is composed of two elements, which are indistinguishable but heterogeneous: one saturated and one with lacunae, the ‘now’ and the not-now, the act and the potential. The lacuna-filled (unrealised, potential) inlay of the
is, indeed, pre-history. If the reader will indulge a paradoxical formula, we might say that the historicity of experience postulates the permanence of pre-history within history. And vice versa:

children: the idea of an ‘end of History’

en: derives from the apparent liquidation or overcoming of pre-history. A wholly saturated series of actions and passions, one that
is thus free of the disorientation of old, would not have any historical tonality, but would fully converge with the ‘becoming an animal again’ whose advent Kojève once heralded.
zh: 前历史是每个亲历时刻都不可缺少、无法避免的方面。同缺乏任何不变环境生态位相联的先行迷失方向与不确定处境，从来不会停止显示自身。此外，它还在自己的时间中确立这样一个事实：每个单一历史时刻都由两个不可分离却又异质的要素组成，一个饱和，一个布满缺口；一个是‘现在’，一个是非现在；一个是实现，一个是潜能。历史时刻布满缺口——未实现、潜在——的镶嵌部分，事实上就是前历史。如果读者愿意容忍一个悖论公式，我们可以说，经验的历史性设定前历史永久存留于历史之中。反过来也一样：‘历史终结’观念源自前历史表面上的清除或克服。一系列完全饱和、因而摆脱古老迷失方向的行动与激情，不会具有任何历史调性，而会同科耶夫曾经宣告其来临的‘重新变成动物’完全汇合。
body.review: 校订疑点 S7：英文为 indistinguishable but heterogeneous；暂据全书一贯论证改为‘不可分离却又异质’，待其他版本复核。

en: Labour-power incarnates the

that cannot be located in the calendar, the pre-historic side of human praxis. There should be no astonishment on account of this formulation. Like all other faculties, the capacity to labour amounts to a

. As we know, potential is the dateless ‘back then’ which accompanies each ‘now’, the incomputable anteriority against which any presence stands out, the indefinite ‘before’ with respect to which the act always appears as an ‘after’. But labour-power, unlike all the other faculties, also enjoys an indisputable empirical prominence: a use-value which is bought and sold, the cornerstone of capitalist accumulation. So it is precisely and only labour-power that makes the non-chronological past carnal and external; that makes the

play an authoritative role in modern political economy; that gives an immediate social significance to the pre-historic lack of specialised instincts. The nebulous ‘other then’ (which does not correspond to any specific epoch) in which the philosophers of the eighteenth century located the origin of language is materialised in capitalism with the physiognomic traits of labour-power.
zh: 劳动力使无法在历法中定位的 illud tempus、使人类实践的前历史一面取得肉身。这个表述不应令人惊讶。同其他一切官能一样，劳动能力等同于一种非年代过去。我们知道，潜能是伴随每个‘现在’而没有日期的‘那时’，是一切在场从中凸显的无法计算之在先性，是实现相对于它总显得是‘之后’的那个不确定‘之前’。但不同于其他一切官能，劳动力还享有无可争辩的经验显著性：它是被买卖的使用价值，是资本主义积累的基石。因此，恰恰也只有劳动力，才使非年代过去成为有血肉的外在存在，使 illud tempus 在现代政治经济学中扮演权威角色，使前历史的专门本能缺失取得直接社会意义。十八世纪哲学家把语言起源安置其中的朦胧‘另一个那时’——它不对应任何特定时代——在资本主义中以劳动力的面貌特征物质化。

en: The capitalist mode of production joins together three different temporal dimensions: a) the labour carried out months or years before, crystallised in money, or rather in monetary capital; b) the potential to labour, that is, the pre-historic
; c) the labour that is actually underway, which appertains to the ‘now’. In the exchange between money and labour-power two radically dissimilar

‘nows’ are at play, one of them dateable (the already-objectified labour, combining to form capital) and the other extraneous to chronology (the faculty as such). It is not the past and present that meet on the market, as Marx himself sometimes suggests,
but rather two
. The labour that is actually underway, the only labour that merits being considered

, will make its appearance only later, within the production process. However, that which follows the exchange conceals the terms of the question. The two ‘nows’, which are at first counterposed, overlap until they become just one. When the buying and selling are over, no trace of labour-power remains. Objectified labour – capital – intersects and absorbs ‘labour as subjectivity’. The chronological past (the sum of previous actualities) latches onto the non-chronological past (pre-historic potential), assimilates it to itself, imposes its own features on it, and becomes its legitimate representative. Behind the labour now underway (the present) there seems only to be a chain of already-accomplished labours, only the ‘dead labour’ concentrated in the hands of the capitalist; the other antecedent, the
for production, seems to
have been wiped from the horizon. The explicit manifestation of the

is overturned as it is eclipsed. It is here (or also here, at least) that the semblance that pre-history has been definitively overcome lays its roots. And the presumed liquidation of pre-history, as we have seen, leads to the belief that History itself has reached the end of the line.
zh: 资本主义生产方式把三个不同时间维度联结起来：（a）几个月或几年前实行、结晶为货币——更准确地说，结晶为货币资本——的劳动；（b）劳动潜能，即前历史的 illud tempus；（c）实际正在进行、属于‘现在’的劳动。在货币与劳动力的交换中，两种根本不同的‘那时’发生作用：一种可以标定日期——结合起来形成资本的、已经对象化的劳动；另一种处于年代之外——官能本身。市场上相遇的不是马克思本人有时暗示的过去与当下，

而是两种不同过去。实际正在进行、唯一配被视作当下的劳动，要到后来才在生产过程中出现。然而，交换之后发生的事情遮蔽了这一问题中的各个关系项。起初彼此对置的两个‘那时’相互重叠，直至合而为一。买卖结束后，劳动力不留任何痕迹。对象化劳动——资本——同‘作为主体性的劳动’交叉并把它吸收。年代过去——此前现实性的总和——攫住非年代过去——前历史潜能——把后者同化于自身，把自身特征强加给它，并成为它的合法代表。在眼下正在进行的劳动——当下——背后，似乎只有一连串已经完成的劳动，只有集中在资本家手中的‘死劳动’；另一个前项——生产官能——似乎已经从视域中抹去。illud tempus 的明确显现，在遭到遮蔽时被颠倒。前历史已被彻底克服的表象，正是在这里——至少也在这里——扎下根来。而我们已经看到，前历史已经被清除这一假定，导致人相信历史本身已走到终点。
body.review: 校订疑点 S8：英文两处为 two … ‘nows’；本段明确区分两种过去，译文沿用两个‘那时’。

en: The historical materialist recognises that the true emblem of capitalism, from the temporal perspective, is the
. But she gives this expression an extremely radical meaning: the equally concrete, non-contemporaneous moments that coexist in the capitalist mode of production are pre-history and actuality, the
and the present that is now underway. The lacuna-filled element of the lived instant (the age-old lack of a pre-fixed environment) emerges in social and economic relations

its saturated element (fully determinate actions). However, it does not cease to be what it is (potential, lacuna-filled) merely on account of having obtained an external, practical aspect. The materialist knows that the empirical incarnation of pre-history does not imply that it has been overcome, but, on the contrary, demonstrates its persistence. The materialist, then, takes seriously the contemporaneity of the non-contemporaneous. And within this, she sees a point of no return. It has become simply impossible to conceive of a historical praxis that does not have to engage closely with the enduring interconnection between pre-history and actuality (that is, with the condition that makes history itself possible). Needless to say, this is all the more true for any praxis that seeks to establish an intransigent critique of capitalism.
zh: 历史唯物主义者认识到，从时间视角看，资本主义真正的标志是非同时者的同时代性。但她赋予这个表达一种极其根本的含义：在资本主义生产方式中共存而彼此非同时、又同样具体的时刻，是前历史与现实性，是 illud tempus 与眼下正在进行的当下。亲历瞬间中布满缺口的要素——自古以来对预先固定环境的缺乏——同它的饱和要素——得到充分规定的行动——一道出现于社会经济关系中。然而，它并不会仅仅因为取得外在实践面貌，就不再是它自身——潜在、布满缺口。唯物主义者知道，前历史在经验中取得肉身并不意味着它已被克服；相反，这恰恰证明它持续存在。因此，唯物主义者严肃对待非同时者的同时代性，并在其中看到一个不可逆转点。现在已经根本不可能设想一种历史实践，可以不必紧密应对前历史与现实性之间持久的相互联结——也就是使历史本身成为可能的条件。不言而喻，对任何力求对资本主义作出不妥协批判的实践而言，这一点更是如此。
黑格尔，《历史哲学讲演录》，§69以下，marxists.org。

zh: 例如：‘对象化劳动，即在空间中在场的劳动，也可以作为过去劳动，同在时间中在场的劳动相对立。如果劳动要在时间中在场、要活着，那么它只能作为活的主体而在场；在这个主体中，它作为能力、作为可能性而存在。’（马克思，《政治经济学批判大纲》，第5章）对象化劳动是过去劳动，这一点毫无疑问。但它真能同某种当下之物相对立吗？依照马克思的说法，在场的是‘活劳动’；然而在交换时刻，后者‘作为能力、作为可能性而存在’。单纯的劳动能力，绝不等同于一项实际正在进行的现实劳动。劳动（还）不在场；在场的是工人的‘直接身体存在’，或者说，是作为劳动力基底的生命。开个玩笑，我们可以说，在交换时刻，‘活劳动’这个词的形容词已经在场，名词却（还）没有……
en: For example,
labour, i.e. labour which is
, can also be opposed, as
, to labour which is
. If it is to be present in time, alive, then it can be present only as the
, in which it exists as capacity, as possibility’ (Marx,

, Chapter 5). Objectified labour is past labour; no doubt, on this score. But can it really be opposed to something present. According to Marx, it is ‘living labour’ which is present; yet at the moment of exchange, this latter ‘exists as capacity, as possibility’. And the mere capacity for labour is not at all the same thing as an actual labour that is really underway. Labour is (still) not present, but the ‘immediate bodily existence’ of the worker, or life as the substratum of labour-power, is. We might say, in jest, that at the moment of exchange the adjective of ‘living labour’ is present, but not (yet) the noun …
